text:
Cheng: Heads-up — noticed a quota spike for tenant `acme-dev` this morning but the routing decision logs show requests routed to `exp-model-v2` while billing reports attribute tokens to `default-model`. Digging in now, but wondering if header normalization or sampling is hiding the real path.
Maya: ugh. Is this the same tenant that had header-casing fun last month? :grimacing: any quick query we can run to compare decision_log.route_id vs billing.model_id?
Cheng: running a replay now against the sampled decision logs. If sampling missed a small fraction of requests that triggered the override, we could be misattributing at scale. Command I'm using: `SELECT route_id, header_x_model, count(*) FROM decision_logs WHERE tenant='acme-dev' GROUP BY 1,2;`
Alex: Can you paste a small example of the raw request header where we see mismatch? I want to check if the gateway overwrote `x-model` after routing.
Cheng: snippet from a captured request: ```
Host: api.redwood.prod
X-Model: exp-model-v2
X-Tenant: acme-dev
User-Agent: curl/7.79.1
```
Cheng: but the response headers we see in billing traces look like: ```
X-Model: default-model
X-Billing-Model: default-model
```
Sophie: that suggests an in-flight override after route eval. Maybe the fallback policy in the prioritizer rewrote `x-model` when the selected pool was full. We have a code path that sets `response_header['X-Model']=fallback_model` for soft-fallbacks.
Maya: is that intended to affect billing? We intended billing to use the original matched route_id not the final response header. If the billing pipeline pulls the model from response headers, that's a bug.
Alex: quick grep shows `billing-service` reads model id from `request.headers['x-model'] || response.headers['x-model']` — so yes, it prefers response header if present.
Cheng: which means if runtime override happens (e.g., autoscale cold-start fallback), billing will attribute to fallback. Because decision logs are sampled at 1% for high-volume tenants, we might not have enough decision logs to correlate.
Sophie: two action items: 1) short-term — change billing-service to prefer the original decision log route_id if present; fall back to request header only if decision log absent. 2) medium term — add a persistent `x-routing-id` to responses so billing + tracing can always correlate even when headers are mutated.
Maya: agree. Also we should increase decision_log sampling for tenants that cross a quota threshold so we get full coverage during spikes.
Alex: I can open a tiny patch for billing-service to prefer `decision_log.route_id`. Will add a guard and unit test.
deploy-bot: deploy queued by @Alex for billing-service (canary). Change diff: prefer_decision_log_route_id boolean (default true).
Cheng: Thanks. For observability, can we add a quick console panel that shows "requests where route_id != billing_model" sampled over last 24h? Would be helpful to catch these sooner.
Sophie: yep, I'll add a kpi in the routing dashboard: sample-match-rate = count(decision_log where route_id == billing_model) / count(decision_log). Also make an alert if sample-match-rate drops below 98% for >15m.
Maya: follow-up: we should audit any other services that read model id from response headers. Might be more places.
Alex: will grep the monorepo and raise a ticket for owners where found.
Cheng: one more note — let's make the decision_log include the `effective_pool` and `fallback_reason` fields even when sampled so a single sample gives enough context. That should reduce investigation time.
Sophie: agreed. I'll bake that into the decision-log schema change. We'll keep sampling rate same but sample richer records.
Maya: cool. Thanks team — fingers crossed this explains the spike. :crossed_fingers:
Alex: patch merged to canary, rolling now. I'll post canary results in this thread in ~10m.
deploy-bot: billing-service canary healthy (3/3 instances).
Alex: canary looks good, no regressions. Leaving config toggle to Ops to flip to prod after hour of monitoring.
Cheng: great. Leaving this open until dashboard + schema changes land. Cheers.
